claims.text: Lamplit Labs reduced cost per merged PR for coding agents from $31 to $9 over eight weeks while the merge rate of agent PRs stayed between 60% and 67%.
Lamplit Labs defines cost per merged PR as total model spend attributed to agent runs divided by the agent-authored pull requests that actually landed.
In one week of Lamplit Labs run logs, 6% of agent runs consumed 48% of tokens, and almost all of those runs ended with a PR closed without merging or no PR at all.
Lamplit Labs set a per-task token budget declared in the task via .agents/budgets.yml: default 400k input and 60k output tokens, docs 150k/30k, bugfix 400k/60k, feature 900k/120k.
Lamplit Labs' runner tells the agent at 80% of budget to open a PR with what it has or write a handoff note; about a third of near-cap runs now land a smaller PR instead of nothing.
Lamplit Labs added a retry cap: after three failures of the same test command with the same failing test names, the runner refuses to run it again and tells the agent to change approach or stop.
Lamplit Labs added a context-size guard that truncates tool results over 12 KB to the first and last 4 KB, cutting per-pass input tokens on test-heavy tasks by roughly 60%.
At Lamplit Labs, the budget cap fired on only 4% of runs by week 8; the retry cap and context guard did most of the cost reduction and the budget acts as a backstop.
Lamplit Labs' week-8 figures were 58 agent PRs opened, 39 merged (67%), $351 spend, $9 per merged PR, versus week 1 with 49 opened, 30 merged (61%), $930 spend, $31 per merged PR.
Lamplit Labs' waste ratio (share of spend in runs that did not merge) fell from 48% to 17%, and median passes per task fell from 7.8 to 3.4.

Lamplit Labs alerts when the 7-day cost per merged PR rises more than 30% over the 28-day value, and found per-agent budgets failed because docs and feature tasks needed different caps, so budgets belong in the task.
Git AI reports an average cost per merged PR of $14.20 across 312 merged PRs in the last 30 days, down 37% from $22.40 six months earlier.
DigiUsher reported a fully allocated cost of $52.55 per merged PR for a 1,000-engineer firm, based on 77 agent sessions joined to shipped code within seven days.
The DigiUsher customer had a 96.8% cache-hit rate and a blended rate of $0.75 per million tokens across six model classes.
Microsoft's TokenOps enforces one shared run-scoped budget through a shared ledger; a bug where each process kept its own counter let a $2 run cap effectively allow $4 across two agents.

TokenOps's cost_guard policy steers cheaper (downgrades model, trims) once per run when spend crosses about 80% of budget, pre_call_worst_case caps output or halts if the next call's worst case won't fit, and cost_budget halts at the cap.
TokenOps reported mean cost per completed run 78.9% lower than no governance ($0.068 to $0.014) and within-cap success rising from 67% to 96% (18/27 to 26/27), on N=27 scored trials.

Microsoft's TokenOps authors argue gateways such as LiteLLM, Portkey and Cloudflare AI Gateway meter per request or key, whereas an agent run spans many requests, so budgets need a run id carried through the execution graph.

Vanja Petreski's guide recommends per-task budget reservations (routine task $5, hard debug $25, migration $100) with thresholds at 50% (reassess), 80% (freeze new fan-out, require escalation) and 100% (checkpoint and pause).

The guide recommends tracking cost per merged PR (paired with change size and rollback rate), cost per accepted task, retry-waste %, cache-read ratio, flagship-token share and escalation precision, with attribution by task, PR, and team tags.

The guide says to order prompt context most-stable-first and put volatile content last because caching is a prefix game; one cache write plus one read costs 1.35× versus 2× for two uncached uses at 0.1× read and 1.25× write rates.

Accenture's preprint estimates a cache-safe router that routes at session start, in side lanes and at subagent launch recovers 14 to 21% of model spend ($3.3M to $5.0M a year) in an emulated 10,000-seat enterprise at Anthropic list prices of 21 September 2026.

The preprint derives that a mid-task model switch must earn back cache writes: on Anthropic's sheet, Fable 5.1 to Sonnet 5 pays back after 291 requests with return (46 without), and Opus 5 to Sonnet 5 after 27 (8 without).
The preprint finds that because Fable 5.1 cache reads cost $0.25 per million tokens versus $0.50 for Opus 5, the highest-priced model can cost less than the next tier on long tool-heavy sessions.
amux's FinOps guide suggests per-agent-session token caps, such as 500K tokens for an implementation agent, with the agent pausing and alerting the developer at the cap.
